title: riff-trace-request-brief-and-mini-experiments-2026-11-30
body:
Executive summary:

This is a compact synthesis of recent customer asks pulled from support tickets, field calls, and pilot telemetry. Purpose is to: (1) surface low-effort, high-impact quickpatches we can validate in 1 sprint, (2) capture a set of linked asks that point to the same root cause (so eng/product can consider a single fix), and (3) propose lightweight experiments to reduce false-positive regressions in quality metrics.

Method / sources:
- Time window: 2026-11-01 through 2026-11-22.
- Sources: 28 support threads (Zendesk exports), 6 customer calls (notes attached in Confluence link), telemetry spikes from hosted-api region eu-west-1 (latency traces), and two Dedicated customer incident reports.
- Heuristic: group by observable cause (latency, token cost, hallucination, API ergonomics, auth/tenant isolation).

Representative customer quotes (verbatim snippets):
- "We see a cliff at ~512 tokens — p95 jumps from 120ms to 420ms; this breaks streaming playback." (media-saas pilot)
- "When we enable prefix caching we still pay nearly full token cost for short completions. Feels like cache isn't used for partial prompts." (enterprise-Fintech)
- "Tool calling is great but our logs are huge; can we get structured envelope only?" (analytics startup)

Top 6 asks (short labels + short problem statement):
1) streaming-p95-cliff: p95 latency spike at mid-sequence lengths, breaks UX streaming.
   - Source signals: telemetry heatmap, customer calls x3.
   - Impact: high (user-visible), reproducible.
   - Quickpatch candidate: reduce default batch window for streams to 8ms for models with seq variance (config flag).
   - Linked tickets: CS-4981, runtime PR #1021.

2) prefix-cache-trim: customers want cheaper short completions when prefix cache present.
   - Problem: current billing+cache visibility charges customers for full generation even when KV cache hits most tokens.
   - Quickpatch candidate: surface a billing estimate toggle in API and a server-side short-path that subtracts cached-token costs for heuristics.
   - Complexity: medium (billing + backend change + docs).

3) structured-tool-quiet-mode: reduce verbose logging for tool call payloads.
   - Customers asking to toggle between full payload logging and structured envelopes only.
   - Quickpatch: add per-route logging-level config in Console (checkbox) and a short-term server parameter to redact heavy tool args.

4) tenant-auth-grace: ephemeral token refresh failures causing 401 storms with retries.
   - Notes: two Dedicated customers saw auto-scaling cold starts cause transient auth errors.
   - Quickpatch: implement soft-retry with jitter and an alert hook to SRE rather than immediate 429 waterfall.

5) embed-cost-clarity: confusion around per-embedding unit vs batch pricing.
   - Customer asks: sample math in Console is unclear for mixed-dimension batches.
   - Quickpatch: add an inline calculator and two simple examples (1 small batch, 1 large) in the embed page.

6) rerank-debug-hooks: customers request richer trace ids for embedding+reresults to map input->reranked outputs.
   - Quickpatch: add an optional trace header (x-rw-trace) that the customer can opt-into to receive per-step IDs.

Cross-cutting root causes we observed:
- Observability gap: customers can see token-level cost but not easily map it to cached vs compute tokens.
- Default runtime heuristics assume uniform sequence lengths; when traffic is bi-modal streaming UX breaks.
- Logging ergonomics: structured vs verbose needs an on/off control per customer or per-route.

Prioritization + impact heuristic (RICE-style quick score):
- streaming-p95-cliff: Reach=high, Impact=high, Confidence=medium => Sprint-1 candidate.
- prefix-cache-trim: Reach=medium, Impact=high, Confidence=low => Sprint-2 prototype.
- structured-tool-quiet-mode: Reach=medium, Impact=medium, Confidence=high => Hotfix + Console toggle.

Mini experiments (1-3 week):
- EXP-01 streaming-window-tweak: deploy reduced batch window for a single canary tenant and measure p50/p95, abort if errors increase. Linked: CS-4981.
- EXP-02 billing-visible-cache: include a prototype toggle that reports an estimated cached-token discount in API response metadata for 200 calls and collect customer feedback.
- EXP-03 trace-header-opt-in: ship x-rw-trace header for internal pilot customers and capture correlation telemetry; validate privacy/PII concerns.

Engineering notes / costs (rough):
- streaming-window-tweak: small runtime change + canary infra -> 2 engineer-weeks (including tests).
- billing-visible-cache: needs billing engineering + runtime hook + Console UI -> 4-6 engineer-weeks.
- structured-tool-quiet-mode: server-side redaction flag + Console toggle -> 1.5 engineer-weeks.

Dependencies / risks:
- Any change to billing metadata requires signoff from Finance (possible billing reconciliation exposure).
- Prefix caching heuristics touch Durable KV paths; must validate that half-hit scenarios don't undercharge or leak cached keys.
- Trace headers must be opt-in and scrub sensitive tool args to avoid PII leak.

Proposed next steps (owner + due date):
- Owner: Maya Thompson (CS) to schedule triage sync with runtime and billing owners. (Due: 2026-12-03)
- Action: ENG (Miguel Ortiz) to estimate EXP-01 and prepare canary toggle. (Due: 2026-12-07)
- Action: Product (Priya Nair) to draft Console toggle copy and UX flows for structured logging toggle + billing estimator. (Due: 2026-12-10)
- Action: Legal/Security quick consult on trace header PII policy (Jonah Kim). (Due: 2026-12-05)

Open questions for triage:
- Billing: Can we safely present a cached-token discount as an estimate without creating expectation mismatch? (Finance input required)
- Runtime: Are there hidden interactions between reduced batch window and throughput/cost that will cause regressions?
- Support: What guidance should CS give to customers who ask for temporary rollbacks?

Appendix - short raw snippets from tickets (anonymized):
- TKT-9912: "p95 jump at 520 tokens, playlist stalls"
- TKT-9938: "embedding batch math doesn't match invoice"
- TKT-9970: "too many tool args stored in logs, search cost skyrockets"

Notes to self / conversational fragments we left in the doc while collecting feedback:
- "Is the prefix billing problem unique to a few big banks or general? need sample extraction."
- "Could we prototype billing-visible-cache as a response header first? smallest blast radius."

Summary: multiple customers pointing at a small set of runtime and observability gaps. Several low-risk quickpatches can be validated in a single sprint; billing changes will require governance but could materially reduce customer angst and support load. Recommend Sprint-1 focus on streaming-window-tweak + structured-tool-quiet-mode as immediate wins, and queue billing-visible-cache as a scoped project for the next cycle.

-- end of brief --

Revision log:
- 2026-11-24: initial draft (Maya).
- 2026-11-27: added EXP-02 details and PR link to runtime team (Miguel).
- 2026-11-30: updated prioritization after customer call with Fintech pilot (Priya).
